facts.claim: GOES layers in EPSG:3857 use 256 px tiles: GeoColor at GoogleMapsCompatible_Level7 (TileMatrix 0-7), Band13 at Level6 (0-6). BlueMarble Level8; VIIRS Level9.
facts.value: 256 px; GeoColor max TileMatrix 7; Band13 max 6

facts.claim: EPSG:4326 GOES sets are 512 px: GeoColor TMS '1km', Band13 TMS '2km'; at TileMatrix 5 the matrix is 40x20 (9 degrees per tile).
Tile URL template (GOES 3857). Time is YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ; VIIRS uses YYYY-MM-DD; BlueMarble has no Time dimension.
Update period in the Time dimension: PT10M for the four GOES layers in both projections; P1D for VIIRS.
Earliest start in the capabilities Time list: GOES-East GeoColor, GOES-East Band13, GOES-West GeoColor, GOES-West Band13 (3857). Each GOES layer lists exactly 100 ranges, so the list looks capped.
VIIRS listed range: NOAA-20 2018-01-05 to 2026-10-17 (dimension default 2026-10-17); SNPP 2015-11-24 to 2026-10-16 (default 2026-10-16).

Montana tile index: z5 for lon -110, lat 47 is col x=6, row y=11 (formula col=floor((lon+180)/360*2^z), row=floor((1-ln(tan(lat)+sec(lat))/pi)/2*2^z)); equal to the Web-Mercator metre formula. Bounds lon -112.5 to -101.25, lat 40.98 to 48.92: the tile does not reach Montana's 49.00 N edge.
facts.evidence: computed in fetch script; tile bounds checked

facts.claim: Newest frame that returns imagery at check 01:51:26Z (tile probe, not capabilities). Each of the four layers returns 404 for every time after the newest frame.
facts.value: GeoColor East 01:10Z (41 min old); Band13 East 01:20Z (31 min); GeoColor West 01:20Z (31); Band13 West 01:20Z (31)

facts.claim: GIBS says GeoColor has about 40 min latency and updates every 10 min. Our probe measured 31-41 min, consistent with it.

The capabilities document is stale and copies disagree. GOES-East GeoColor default: 01:00Z (copy at 01:48:10Z, age 61 s), 01:10Z (01:48:11Z, age 348 s), 00:30Z (01:51:58Z, age 1259 s). Use tile probes, not capabilities, for 'latest'.
facts.value: up to ~50 min disagreement between copies

facts.claim: Tile responses for times that do not exist: HTTP 404 (text/html, 196 bytes) for future times and for a gap (GOES-West GeoColor 01:00Z). The request for 01:05Z and 01:09Z is HTTP 200 but returns the 01:00Z bytes (off-grid times silently map to the earlier frame).
facts.value: 404 for future and gaps; 200 with previous frame for off-grid

facts.claim: Montana z5 tile content (3857, 256x256): GeoColor East 01:00Z has 4131 distinct RGB; Band13 East 01:20Z has 953; GeoColor West 01:10Z 4480; Band13 West 01:10Z 1014. All 100% non-transparent (GeoColor) or opaque. Each passes the imagery test.
facts.evidence: PIL decode of tiles listed in urls_checked

facts.claim: The VIIRS NOAA-20 layer's default date (2026-10-17, today) returns an all-black tile at this location (1 distinct colour). The previous day (2026-10-16) has 11062 colours. The default date is not a valid frame.
facts.value: default date black; prior day valid

facts.claim: CORS: every tile GET sent with an Origin header returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (3857 GOES, BlueMarble, VIIRS, 4326, Billings). The no-Origin control and the OPTIONS preflight (200) also return *. Both capabilities files return *.
GeoColor native resolution: 1 km at the satellite sub-point for the visible band; full-disk scan every 10 min in Mode 6 operations.
Band 13 native pixel resolution: 2 km at sub-satellite point. Table is in the PDF text layer only; the rendered page did not show it.
GIBS catalog latency categories: NRT = generated within 3.5 h of observation; STD = within 24 h. Which category the GOES layers use is unverified (catalog gated).

GIBS archive depth in the tile service: GOES-East Band13 frames 404 on 2025-06-15 (all probed times, zooms 2-5) and on 2026-07-15 12:00Z; 200 on 2026-07-18 12:00Z and 2026-07-22. Served archive therefore starts between 2026-07-16 and 07-18, earlier than the capabilities list (07-23).
facts.evidence: tile probes listed in urls_checked and limits

facts.claim: Domains service vs tile server disagree for June 2025: the Domains XML lists PT10M segments for 2025-06 (including 2025-06-15), but every tested 2025-06 tile returned 404.
Parallax correction: no GIBS, Earthdata or GeoColor page read mentions parallax, perspective or viewing geometry. Unverified whether GIBS GOES imagery is parallax-corrected.
facts.evidence: text search of nine GIBS/Earthdata pages read

facts.claim: Satellite identity: NOAA guide v1.3 (9/8/2025) gives GOES-19 as operational GOES-East and GOES-18 as GOES-West. The GIBS GeoColor article names GOES-16/17 (older). Which satellite each GIBS layer uses is unverified.

Derived (not stated by GIBS): 3857 pixel size = ScaleDenominator x 0.00028 m. GeoColor Level7 max (4,367,830) is about 1.22 km per pixel at the equator; Band13 Level6 max (8,735,660) about 2.45 km. Assumes the OGC 0.28 mm convention.

terms.license: Mixed. GOES imagery: NOAA NODD terms ('open to the public', attribution requested, no endorsement implied). NASA ESDIS content: 'generally not copyrighted'; NASA-led mission data CC0 unless marked; non-NASA data follow the sponsor's license. GIBS asks for an acknowledgment, not a licence. Our reading: GIBS layers are not licensed separately on the pages read; per-layer sponsor (NOAA, USGS, etc.) unverified.
terms.quote: GIBS: 'NASA promotes full and open sharing of data. We ask that users who make use of GIBS in their clients ... to add the following acknowledgment: We acknowledge the use of imagery provided by services from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), part of NASA's Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS).' | NASA: 'NASA data are freely accessible; however, when you publish these data or works based on the data, we request that you cite the datasets ...' | NASA: 'Non-NASA data available through the ESDIS project is subject to the license arrangements of the sponsoring organization.' | NOAA: 'NOAA data disseminated through NODD are open to the public and can be used as desired.'

limits: One snapshot: capabilities fetched 01:48Z, tiles 01:50-01:52Z, archive probes 02:01-02:02Z (2026-10-17 UTC). Frame numbers move every 10 min; re-run before relying on them.
Imagery test is automated (PIL: transparency, distinct RGB, luma SD). No tile was viewed by eye. 'verified: true' means the bytes were read and decoded, or the status and body were observed.
Coverage: one z5 tile per layer covers only part of Montana (lon -112.5 to -101.25, lat 40.98 to 48.92). Montana (lon -116.05 to -104.04) needs at least two tiles across.
CORS was tested with curl using Origin http://127.0.0.1:8080. No browser test here (rule 8 applies at the UI phase).

Usage: no general rate limit or quota found on the pages read. Bulk download is defined as more than 1,000,000 tiles in 24 h (contact GIBS 48 h ahead); guidance is 50 Mbps sustained and 500 threads. This check made about 120 requests to gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov.
Quotes come from raw HTML or PDF text pulled with curl and parsed locally, not from model summaries. WebSearch was used only to find URLs.

The Earthdata wiki Visualization Product Catalog (per-layer resolution and latency) redirects to Earthdata Login. A search snippet cites a GOES-East ABI row at 1 km image, 0.5 km sensor, 10 min; not verified here.
GIBS frame time labels: the docs do not say whether the label is scan start, scan end or processing time. Compare with NOAA AWS scan times in W2.
Off-grid times return the previous frame with HTTP 200. The globe must label each frame with the time the server actually returned (check bytes), not the requested time.
open_questions: Which satellite feeds each GIBS GOES layer now (GOES-19/18 per NOAA vs GOES-16/17 in the GIBS article)? Cross-check against NOAA AWS bucket timestamps (W2).
Does GIBS parallax-correct GOES imagery? No page says so. Ask earthdata-support@nasa.gov (the address on the bulk-download page) or read the gated product catalog.
Why do Domains say 2025-06 frames exist while tiles 404? Archive depth for a past-storm replay is unknown until GIBS replies.
GOES row of the Visualization Product Catalog (native resolution, latency class NRT/STD): needs Earthdata Login.
Sponsor licence for VIIRS and BlueMarble layers was not checked (NASA CC0 vs non-NASA). Needed before a public release.
